messages:
incident-bot: Pager: KV cache eviction storm detected in us-west-2 (high p50 latency, 5xx uplift). PagerDuty -> oncall-sre. Auto-escalation timer started. :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: got the page, pulling logs now. seeing huge prefetch hits on rope sliding-window keys, burst of unique prefixes.
kevin: logs?
oncall-sre: tail from proxy: 
```
 2026-03-15T03:12:15Z ERROR kv: cache_miss=1.2M prefetch_queue=48k eviction_rate=14k/s active_keys=4.2M
 2026-03-15T03:12:16Z WARN  batcher: continuous_batch_window_ms=1200 inflight_batches=960
 ```
maria: confirmed spike correlated with recent longctx rolling enable (sliding-window prefetch=on) — deployment 2026-03-15T02:55 by ryan-dev.
sanjay: is this NTK path or YaRN prefetch?
oncall-sre: both. rope runtime picking NTK variant, YaRN adaptive prefetch increased kv fanout; combination amplified active key cardinality.
emily: customer impact? any error pages reported?
cs-bot: Incoming CS alerts: 7 customers reported degraded generation latency >5s in last 10m, none have timeouts yet. Ticket backlog increment +12.
kevin: quick mitigation plan: 1) disable sliding-window prefetch rollout (flag rollback) 2) reduce continuous_batch_window to 200ms 3) scale down NTK model pool to limiting variant 4) apply temporary max_prefetch_per_request=8 to YaRN
oncall-sre: executing step 1 now: `./infra/flags rollback --flag=sliding_window_prefetch --env=prod-us-west-2`
incident-bot: Rollback triggered by oncall-sre at 03:13:10Z. Canary checks running.
ryan-dev: i just reverted the feature flag; pushing hotpatch to routing to force prefetch multiplier=1 for new requests. patch id: hp-9042
maria: patch applied to 40% of nodes; seeing steady drop in active_keys on those nodes. evictions per second on canary dropped 60%
kevin: applying batcher config change: `kubectl set env deployment/rope-batcher BATCH_WINDOW_MS=200 -n inference-prod`
oncall-sre: batch window change rolled, inflight_batches down from 960 -> 210 in 45s, p50 latency reduced ~35%
emily: notifying affected customers with preliminary note: short delay expected while we mitigate. cs channel on standby.
cs-bot: Draft message posted to cs team thread.
sanjay: we should also consider short-term cache eviction policy tweak: increase LRU eviction aggressiveness for rope keyspace to free hot shards. kevin ok to apply?
kevin: applying: `redis-cli -h kv-evict-01 config set maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` to sticky cache cluster for rope_*. Doing now.
oncall-sre: after LRU tweak, eviction_rate spiked briefly then settled; miss rate normalized.
incident-bot: Auto-scaling of dedicated pool triggered as a fallback: +3 nodes for NTK-limited pool (policy).
ryan-dev: metrics: total requests impacted estimate = 8.3k reqs in window, approx 0.9% of total prod traffic. Severity: Sev2 (user-visible latency, no data loss).
emily: putting together SLO impact: 99th latency for text-gen in us-west-2 breached from 1.2s -> 6.8s during peak. Rolling average now at 2.1s after mitigations.
kevin: next steps: 1) keep sliding-window flag off for 2h 2) run offline eval of NTK+YaRN prefetch param space with lower multipliers 3) create hotpatch to make prefetch adaptive by request token-length threshold
maria: create incident timeline and RCA ticket. we should include perf cliff thresholds and a playbook for prefetch rollbacks.
ryan-dev: will open PR with max_prefetch cap and telemetry for prefix-cardinality per request. link: https://git.internal/r/PR/1482
onscall-sre: handoff: i’m staying on for the next 30m; if things look stable, i'll hand to oncall-sre for evening. paging team updated.
emily: cs updates sent, customer impact map updated (IDs listed in private doc).
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). Monitoring in watch for 30m.
kevin: assigning follow-ups: #1 RCA doc (maria), #2 telemetry dashboard for prefix cardinality (sanjay), #3 config safe-guards for sliding-window feature (ryan-dev).
maria: acknowledged, will own RCA and post to postmortems channel when ready.
oncall-sre: closing pager for now, will reopen if metrics degrade. thanks all :heart:
